historical_growth.fcf_basis: owner FCF = reported FCF (OCF - acquisition of PP&E and intangibles) less SBC; interest income not stripped (net-debt company). FY2020 10,044 / FY2022 5,988 / FY2025 2,744 (US$m).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Mid-cycle volume-led growth (iron ore ~335 -> ~350 Mt, copper 360-380 kt rising toward 700 kt by 2035) at a flat real price; the trailing CAGRs run from a US$160/t FY2021 peak (or its FY2020 approach) to a US$93/t FY2025 and measure the commodity cycle, not the business.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All trailing CAGRs are negative and span the 2021 iron-ore price peak to the 2025 trough; EPS CAGRs are further distorted by the FY2025 US$4.6bn nickel impairment. Equity CAGR (-1.3% 5yr) reflects US$30bn+ of dividends and buybacks paid out over 2021-25, not value destruction. None is a usable forward proxy for a cyclical; the selected rate is a volume judgment.
historical_growth.notes: Reported-FCF 3yr/5yr CAGRs are -22.6%/-22.7% - essentially identical to the owner-FCF series because SBC is ~0.1% of revenue. Peak-to-trough: FY2021 owner FCF US$20.6bn vs FY2025 US$2.7bn (the latter also after US$1.25bn of dam/de-characterisation payments, US$0.7bn one-off debenture repurchase and US$1.0bn interest paid inside OCF).

scenario_narratives.base: Iron ore is ~75% of revenue and its price is the valuation. The base case takes the 2026 windfall (~US$105/t, record Carajas output, 335-345 Mt guidance) and mean-reverts to a ~US$90/t realised price by 2028 as Simandou ramps and Chinese steel output drifts below 1 Bt, with Vale growing volumes 2-3%/yr thereafter (Serra Sul +20 from 2H26, Capanema, copper 360-380 kt rising ~6%/yr, nickel flat and Thompson deconsolidated). The cash-conversion-adjusted EBITDA margin troughs at 33.5% (~36% adjusted) in 2028 and recovers to 34.5% as copper mix and the cost programme offset grade decline and the raised US$58-62/t all-in cost. Capex holds near US$5.5bn (13.5-14% of revenue through 2028, 12.5% at maturity, still ~3.5pp above D&A). Cash tax ramps 20% -> 24% as Brazilian incentives and JCP deductibility erode. The dam settlements (Brumadinho, Samarco Definitive Settlement, upstream-dam de-characterisation), the railway-concession liability and NCI are deducted in the bridge at carrying value, so the model charges them once and the forward EBITDA is Vale's pre-Brumadinho adjusted basis. The base case lands near the current price: the market is pricing roughly a US$90/t mid-cycle with the liability stack honoured.
scenario_narratives.bull: Vale's raised US$100/t long-term deck proves right: 50-60 Mtpy of depleting high-cost capacity and tightening Chinese environmental and quality standards keep realised fines at US$100-110/t despite Simandou, with India and Southeast Asia absorbing China's gradual decline and premium Carajas/briquette products earning a widening quality spread. Copper reaches 450-500 kt by 2030 at US$4.50-5.00/lb with strong gold credits, nickel recovers from the Indonesian glut, and the cost and efficiency programme (AI, dry processing, briquetting) delivers rather than merely offsets. Cash-EBITDA settles at 39.5% (~42% adjusted) on revenue compounding ~3%. Capital returns continue (dividends plus the 100m-share buyback) with the dam liabilities now capped and defined. Same 10% WACC - all the upside is in the flows.
scenario_narratives.bear: The China axis breaks the wrong way: Chinese steel output shrinks 2-3%/yr while Simandou adds up to 120 Mtpy of high-grade supply, pushing realised fines to ~US$75/t in 2027-28 and ~US$80/t thereafter - the level at which Vale's freight disadvantage (US$22/t to Asia vs US$10-12/t for the Australians) and raised all-in cost bite hardest. Iron-ore EBITDA/t falls from ~US$45 to ~US$27; a stronger BRL inflates the USD cost base; copper growth slips on permitting and project delays; nickel stays loss-making. Growth capex is cut but ~US$4.6-5.0bn of sustaining spend cannot be, and Samarco funding shortfalls run at the US$1bn/yr cap through 2030 with further Brumadinho individual claims. Cash-EBITDA compresses to 26-28.5% (~29-31% adjusted). Because ~US$17bn of fixed claims (net debt, dam provisions, concession liability) sit ahead of equity, a ~30% lower enterprise value translates into a >60% lower equity value - which is why the bear value is far below the 52-week low even though the business remains solvent and cash-generative throughout.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Vale as an unlevered owner-FCF stream at a USD-built 10% WACC, normalising iron ore to a ~US$90/t mid-cycle rather than extrapolating 2026's ~US$105/t or 2021's US$160/t, converting reported adjusted EBITDA to a cash-EBITDA margin (~2.5pp lower), and charging every fixed claim exactly once in the bridge: net debt including leases, the three dam-related provisions at discounted book, the railway-concession liability and NCI, with equity-accounted investments added back at book. The terminal multiple is capped at 12x owner FCF for a cyclical. The honest finding is that the equity is a levered call on the iron ore price: the claims stack is ~US$17bn, so the bear case is savage even though Vale stays solvent in it.
key_risks_to_valuation: Realised iron ore price: every US$10/t sustained is roughly US$3bn of EBITDA (~US$5/share at the house multiple) - the single input that dominates the range

Dam liabilities: provisions are discounted at 8.2-8.5% real and depend on Samarco self-funding; the 20-F's US$8.4bn undiscounted expected outflow and the US$1bn/yr shortfall cap through 2030 could exceed the US$6.0bn carried
Cash tax: Brazilian income-tax reform and SUDAM/SUDENE expiries could take the cash rate above the 24% terminal assumption
Capex intensity: sustaining capex structurally above D&A; project overruns (Serra Sul +20, Tocantins bridge, copper) or a longer growth tranche would hold capex at 14%+
Cash conversion: the ~2.5pp leakage assumption; a further debenture repurchase or working-capital build in a rising-price year widens it
Brazil governance: golden-share vetoes, CEO/board political pressure, railway-concession renegotiation and dividend/JCP tax changes
BRL appreciation raising the USD cost base (costs, capex and some debt in BRL/CAD against USD revenue)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 10.71-17.94
data_sources.financials: VALE_Metrics.csv / metrics_normalized (FY2015-FY2025 20-F, Q1-2024 to Q2-2026 6-K interims, USD millions); VALE_20F_FY2025.txt (liquidity and capital resources, capex guidance, note 12 impairment, note 32(b) share-based payments); VALE_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt (statement of financial position and cash flows, notes 6, 12, 14, 19, 22, 23, 25)
data_sources.qualitative: VALE_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): guidance items, bull/bear axes, recent developments (Thompson consortium, Alianca sale, Samarco Definitive Settlement, Q2 2026 guidance changes)

inputs.sbc_source: 20-F FY2025 note 32(b) 'Charges related to share-based payments' US$51m (FY2024 US$16m), equity-settled Matching + PSU programs; cross-check: grant-date fair values of the 2023-25 programs straight-lined over 3-year vesting imply ~US$45m/yr. No net-share-settlement taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 in kpis). SBC is 0.13% of revenue - immaterial; history not backfilled into the DB because the filings disclose only grant tables, not an annual expense line.
inputs.buyback_note: H1 FY2026 financing outflow US$214m (8.8m shares in Q2 at ~US$16); FY2025 nil; FY2021-23 US$14.3bn. New 100m-share authorisation (Q2 2026) is an authorisation, not spend.
inputs.share_count_basis: 4,255.76m common shares outstanding ex-treasury at 30-Jun-2026 (Q2 2026 note 25(a); 183.4m treasury shares excluded) plus 6.6m dilutive potential shares (diluted less basic weighted-average, note 6) = 4,262.4m. One NYSE ADS = one common share. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; buybacks are value-neutral under the house method.
inputs.fx_note: Vale reports in USD under IFRS (functional currency of the parent is BRL but presentation currency is USD) and the NYSE ADS quotes in USD; no conversion. The B3 listing (VALE3) quotes in BRL and is not used.
inputs.net_debt_note: Loans and borrowings US$1,093m current + US$17,211m non-current = US$18,304m, plus lease liabilities US$169m + US$465m = US$634m (treatment A, leases as debt) = total_debt US$18,938m. Cash US$5,577m + short-term investments US$188m = US$5,765m. Net debt US$13,173m, all at 30-Jun-2026 (Q2 2026 interim statement of financial position). Excluded from debt on purpose: participative shareholders' debentures (inside 'Other financial liabilities' US$3,247m) because their remuneration (~US$280m/yr) stays inside the flows via the cash-margin haircut; REFIS tax settlement programs (US$1,091m) because their instalments are inside 'Payments of income taxes' and so inside the cash tax rate; streaming liabilities (non-cash deferred revenue); employee benefit obligations (service cost in EBITDA).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are USD, so the rate is built in USD: 10y UST ~4.2% + beta 1.1 x 5.0% ERP = 9.7% market cost of equity, plus 1.5pp jurisdiction premium (roughly half the Brazil sovereign USD spread; Vale's revenue is USD and seaborne but its assets, licences, dams and regulator are Brazilian, and the golden share gives the state governance vetoes) = 11.2% cost of equity. After-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (2054 bond 6.40%, 2056 sub notes 6.00%, Brazilian tax shield). Weights at market: equity US$58.6bn / net debt US$13.2bn -> 82/18. WACC = 0.82 x 11.2 + 0.18 x 5.0 = 10.1%, used as 10.0% in ALL three scenarios. Commodity-price cyclicality is priced in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: A - leases as debt. IFRS 16 lease liabilities (US$634m at 30-Jun-2026: vessels, ports, pelletising plants, properties) are included in total_debt; lease principal (US$83m H1 2026, financing) is NOT deducted from the flows; right-of-use renewal is covered by the capex path. Variable lease payments not in the liability (US$65m H1 2026) are already inside EBITDA.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: equity attributable to non-controlling interests US$935m at 30-Jun-2026 (chiefly Manara Minerals' 10% of Vale Base Metals) deducted at book. Flows are consolidated (100%). NCI's share of profit is small and volatile (FY2025 NCI absorbed part of the nickel impairment: total net income US$1,983m vs attributable US$2,352m), so book is the cleaner single charge.
inputs.dam_liabilities_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge, at the discounted carrying amounts on the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet: Brumadinho US$1,774m (807 current + 967 non-current, note 22), Samarco/Fundao Definitive Settlement US$2,097m ('Liabilities related to associates and joint ventures', 662 + 1,435, note 23 - discounted at 8.20% real), and de-characterisation of upstream dam structures US$2,124m (note 12, the Brumadinho-driven acceleration programme, cash outflows over up to 13 years, discounted at 8.53% real). The forward EBITDA path is Vale's adjusted (pre-Brumadinho-expense) basis, so none of these payments sit in the flows; historical reported FCF DID carry Brumadinho and de-characterisation payments (operating) but NOT Samarco payments (investing), which is why last_fcf is not comparable to the year-1 projection. Cross-check: the 20-F guides US$2,426m of such payments in 2026 and US$5,960m after 2026 (undiscounted); H1 2026 actual payments were US$1,350m (370 Brumadinho + 134 de-characterisation + 846 Samarco). The Samarco figure is a provision for Vale's secondary 50% share of what Samarco cannot self-fund, capped at US$1bn/yr through 2030; a shortfall beyond the provision is a bear-case item. Ordinary asset-retirement obligations (US$3,600m) and environmental obligations (US$427m) are NOT deducted: they are the normal end-of-life closure costs every miner carries, fall largely beyond the horizon, and partly overlap sustaining capex.
inputs.other_bridge_items: Railway concession liability US$2,419m (629 + 1,790, note 14: EFC/EFVM 2020 renewal obligations) deducted because the capex path is anchored on the US$5.4-5.7bn 2026 guidance, which by Vale's definition excludes concession-grant disbursements (those run through the 'acquisition of PP&E and intangibles' line, US$6.0bn in FY2025 vs US$5.5bn capex). Investments in associates and JVs US$5,264m (note 26: MRS, VLI, Baovale, CSI, the 15% Minas-Rio stake, Alianca Energia 30% residual etc.; Samarco carried at nil) ADDED at book under the matching-asset rule - their income is equity-accounted and their dividends (US$63m H1 2026) arrive in investing, so neither is in the flows.
inputs.cash_margin_note: ebitda_margin_path is a CASH-conversion-adjusted margin, not Vale's reported adjusted-EBITDA margin. Reported adjusted EBITDA converts to 'cash generated from operations' at only ~87-91% (FY2024: ~US$13.5bn CGO vs US$14.8bn EBITDA; FY2025: ~US$13.5bn vs US$15.5bn; H1 2026: US$5.6bn vs US$7.5bn, seasonally worse) before interest, tax and dam payments. The persistent part - participative debenture remuneration ~US$280m/yr, inventory and receivable drift, other non-EBITDA operating cash items - is ~2.5pp of revenue. So base-case 'cash EBITDA' 34.5% at maturity = ~37% adjusted EBITDA margin at ~US$90/t realised fines price, against 40.3% in FY2025 (~US$93/t), 39.0% in FY2024 (~US$95/t), 38.0% in H1 2026 (higher price, but all-in cost guidance raised to US$58-62/t).
inputs.normalisation_note: Commodity cyclical: FY2021 (revenue US$54.5bn, EBITDA US$31.2bn at ~US$160/t average) and FY2022 are peak-price years and are not used as an anchor for any driver. Base mean-reverts from ~US$105/t in 2026 (H1 2026 revenue +17% YoY) to ~US$90/t by 2028 as Simandou ramps (c.60-120 Mtpy over 2026-28) and Chinese steel output drifts lower, then grows with volume: iron ore 335-345 Mt (2026 guidance) to ~350 Mt (Serra Sul +20, 2H26), copper 360-380 kt (2026) rising toward the 700 kt 2035 ambition, nickel flat-to-down (Thompson deconsolidates on completion of the consortium deal, expected end-2026; <1% of revenue). Vale's own long-term planning deck was raised to US$100/t in 2026; the base case sits deliberately below it. The FY2025 US$4.6bn impairment (US$1,745m Thompson/other nickel CGUs + US$1,735m Canadian nickel goodwill, FY2025 20-F note 12) is a non-cash write-down of nickel assets on a lower nickel-price deck: one-off in the P&L, but it confirms nickel earns little, which the margin paths already reflect.
inputs.tax_note: Brazilian statutory rate is 34% but Vale's CASH rate on EBIT runs ~16-20% (FY2023-25 cash taxes US$1.9-2.0bn/yr on ~US$12bn EBIT) thanks to SUDAM/SUDENE incentives on Carajas and Northern System profits (through the early 2030s), interest-on-capital (JCP) deductibility and foreign-earnings structure. Base ramps 20% -> 24% by 2031 as the Brazilian income-tax reform (dividend taxation from 2026, pressure on JCP) and incentive expiries bite; bear 20% -> 25%; bull follows base.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted (routing table row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' - owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md read in full). Fresh build; no prior DCF or memory entry. Vale is an operating miner whose value is a stream of unlevered FCF, so the owner-FCF engine applies; the cyclical adaptation is mid-cycle price normalisation in the driver paths (see normalisation_note) rather than any adjustment to the discount rate. Interest income (US$501m FY2025) is NOT stripped because Vale is a net-debt company (cash is netted inside net debt, not added to EV) - the double-count rule does not apply; the unlevered component build excludes financial income anyway. Reported OCF is post interest paid (~US$1.0bn/yr, operating under Vale's IFRS classification), so historical reported FCF is a levered figure; the forward build is unlevered. Working capital: receivables US$2.6bn + inventories US$6.3bn vs payables US$6.2bn -> growth consumes cash, wc_capture_pct = -7 (net operating WC ~7% of revenue). SBC-light market: house and street bases nearly coincide (SBC 0.13% of revenue); band_position will be close to degenerate and should be read as such. Analysis JSON (2026-10-04) was available and read; its guidance items (335-345 Mt, US$58-62/t all-in cost, copper 360-380 kt) and bull/bear axes are reflected in the paths.

bear.rationale: Simandou (120 Mtpy at full rate) lands on a Chinese steel sector shrinking 2-3%/yr; realised fines fall to ~US$75/t in 2027-28 and settle near US$80/t; BRL strength and raised all-in costs (US$58-62/t) compress iron-ore EBITDA/t from ~US$45 to ~US$27; copper growth slips (permits, Bacaba/Alemao delays); growth capex is cut but a ~US$4.6-5.0bn sustaining budget cannot be; Samarco funding shortfalls run at the US$1bn/yr cap. Cash-EBITDA 28.5% = ~31% adjusted (FY2015 at US$55/t was 30% adjusted on a far weaker BRL). With ~US$17bn of fixed claims (net debt + dam provisions + concessions) ahead of equity, a 25-30% EV decline becomes a >50% equity decline - the leverage in this stock is in the claims stack, not the gearing ratio.

base.growth_rationale: 2026 +7% (H1 2026 revenue +17% YoY on ~US$105/t and record Q1 output; H2 laps a strong H2 2025); 2027 -5% and 2028 -2% as realised fines revert to ~US$90/t with Simandou ramping; thereafter volume-led 2-3% (Serra Sul +20 from 2H26, copper +5-7%/yr, Capanema) fading to 2% terminal nominal - below USD inflation, reflecting depletion.
base.margin_rationale: Cash-EBITDA (see inputs.cash_margin_note): 36.0% in 2026 (H1 adjusted 38.0% less ~2.5pp leakage; all-in cost guidance raised to US$58-62/t), 33.5% at the 2028 price trough (~36% adjusted), recovering to 34.5% (~37% adjusted) as copper mix and the cost programme offset grade decline.
base.capex_rationale: US$5.55bn 2026 guidance midpoint = 13.5% of US$41.1bn; 14% in 2027-28 because the dollar budget (~US$5.5bn: Serra Sul +20, Tocantins bridge, Bacaba, Alemao) holds while revenue dips; eases to 12.5% (~US$5.5bn on US$44-45bn) once the growth tranche rolls off - still ~3.5pp above D&A, as sustaining spend on an ageing Southern/Southeastern system structurally exceeds book depreciation.
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 12x owner FCF (method: 12-15x for cyclicals; Vale has traded 4-7x EV/EBITDA through the cycle). Gordon at 10%/2% is 12.75x, so the cap binds marginally.

bull.rationale: Vale's own US$100/t long-term deck proves roughly right and realised fines hold US$100-110/t (depleting Australian/Brazilian capacity of 50-60 Mtpy offsets Simandou; India and SE Asia absorb China's decline); copper reaches 450-500 kt by 2030 at US$4.50-5.00/lb with gold credits; nickel recovers from the Indonesian glut; the cost programme delivers. Cash-EBITDA 39.5% = ~42% adjusted. Same WACC - the upside is in the flows.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.band_position_note: DEGENERATE - read as not applicable. SBC is 0.13% of revenue, so house and street values differ by ~US$0.15/share and the band_position denominator is near zero; the market is simply paying ~US$0.9/share above both bases, not 6x along an SBC band. SBC rows are kept explicit at 0.13% per the house rule rather than zeroed.
probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35. For a price-taking commodity producer the distribution of outcomes around mid-cycle is roughly symmetric, and the asymmetries largely offset: downside tails (structural Chinese steel decline, Simandou, Brazilian political and regulatory interference via the golden share, Samarco funding shortfalls, further dam incidents) argue for bear > bull, while copper optionality and Vale's own higher price deck argue the other way. The bear case's severity in dollars already captures the fixed-claim leverage, so it is not also over-weighted. Bull is capped at 25% because it needs the price deck, copper execution and the cost programme all to go right.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
